entities.summary: Avraham "Bren" Adan was an Israeli major-general and author. Prior to Israel's independence, he served with the Palmach, an elite formation within the Haganah paramilitary force of the Yishuv community in British Mandatory Palestine. Adan fought under the Haganah and later under the newly formed Israel Defense Forces during the First Arab–Israeli War, and was photographed while raising the Israeli Ink Flag at the site of what is now Eilat to mark the end of the war. He served with the Israel Defense Forces from 1948 to 1977, and fought in all of the major Arab–Israeli wars that occurred during that period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Avraham Adan's service in the Palmach and Israel Defense Forces played a significant role in the First Arab–Israeli War, with his photograph raising the Israeli flag at Eilat marking its end. His involvement in major Arab–Israeli wars from 1948 to 1977 highlights his impact on regional security.
